answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using hardware enclave attestation. Each candidate must execute inside a certified enclave, proving its integrity across the consensus ledge with silicon-fused signatures to block hollow software emulators. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of purchasing discrete cryptographic chips, each the size of a walnut, per identity. However, side-channel attacks can leak attestation keys, and reliance on proprietary foundries centralizes trust.
